facts: Heritage-listed shearing shed on Evanslea Road, Jondaryan, built 1859-60 on the former Jondaryan pastoral station (at one time the largest freehold station in Queensland); scene of labour conflict in the late 1880s-early 1890s, a test case for the Queensland Shearers Union before the 1891 shearers' strike

Site also has a recreated 19th-century village and a museum collection; operated by Toowoomba Regional Council; about 30 minutes west of Toowoomba on the Warrego Highway; allow about an hour; caravan park/accommodation on site

facts: Former deep-water cargo pier built 1913-17 (originally 1124 m) to export sugar, timber and coal, served by a railway extension from Pialba; closed 1985, 239 m demolished, 868 m retained after public outcry; last 220 m restored by 2009

Council says the 868 m pier is kept safe for fishing, walking and sightseeing; restoration works from Jan 2025, reopened after coastal protection works (Fraser Coast Regional Council); anglers target whiting; toilets, free parking beside Pier Park (parking not a price)
